unfinished.title: src/fabric/api.py::build -- refuse a magnitude lever that is NaN or +inf. I own nothing and may not edit; this is the exact, TESTED find/replace.
unfinished.reason: I am an independent verifier and edited no file. The defect is in src/fabric/api.py, which is j_fabric's file, not mine. I built the repair in a mirror and ran the suite against it before handing it on.
unfinished.detail:
FIND (src/fabric/api.py, inside build, one occurrence -- anchored on text, not a line number):
    _rev = [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in _applied if v < 0.0]
    _off = [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in _gated_off if v < 0.0]
REPLACE WITH (the two lines are kept, unchanged, after the new block):
    # NOT-A-NUMBER IS NOT A MAGNITUDE EITHER, AND `v < 0.0` IS FALSE FOR IT. Measured at the suite's own
    # widths: FAB_BALANCE=nan assembles with no warning, FAB.build accepts it, aux_loss comes back nan
    # and every gradient-carrying tensor on the population is non-finite -- while fab.balance prints
    # "armed, did not fire (balance=nan x warm=0.9992 vs > 0) -- FAB_BALANCE=nan: no load-balance
    # pressure", which is F1's defect and F7's defect in one rendered line. FAB_PONDER and FAB_EMB_VAR
    # do the same; FAB_DOM_FRAC=nan does not reach a gate at all, it raises a bare ValueError from
    # _breadth_ban. +inf is admitted too. -inf is caught only because it is negative.
    _unreal = [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in _applied + _gated_off if v != v or v == float("inf")]
    if _unreal:
        raise LeverError(
            f"FAB: magnitude lever(s) {', '.join(_unreal)} are not a magnitude. `v < 0.0` is False "
            f"for a NaN and for +inf, so neither is caught by the refusal below.")
    _rev = [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in _applied if v < 0.0]
    _off = [f"{k}={v}" for k, v in _gated_off if v < 0.0]

NOTES FOR WHOEVER LANDS IT. `math` is not imported in this file, which is why the test is `v != v` and `v == float("inf")` rather than math.isfinite. `_applied` and `_gated_off` are both tuples, so `+` concatenates. The message above is the minimum; the owner should decide whether it deserves the same measured paragraph the negative refusal carries.
MEASURED WITH IT APPLIED, in a mirror outside the repo: tests/test_contract.py '=== 16 checks + 77 self-test cases, 0 failing ==='; tests/test_fabric.py '=== 9 checks, 0 failing ==='; FAB_BALANCE=nan and =inf refused by name; FAB_BALANCE=0.0, 1.0, 5.0 and -0.0 all still BUILD, so F7's -0.0 second reading and F4's no-overreach clause are untouched.
WHAT IS NOT COVERED BY IT: FAB_DOM_FRAC=nan's ValueError comes from _breadth_ban during forward and this refusal removes it by making the config unbuildable, which is the right layer -- but there is no check anywhere that would have caught it, and `grep -rn 'isnan\|isfinite' src/` prints nothing, so the same hole plausibly exists in every other package's numeric levers. unfinished.reason: It is an owner's decision and not a measurement, exactly as they said. What I add is that the question they framed as {refuse -0.0 or admit it} is really {what does `v < 0.0` let through}, and the answer I measured is: -0.0, NaN and +inf.
unfinished.detail:
THEIR FRAMING, WHICH STANDS: build refuses at `v < 0.0`; -0.0 is not less than 0.0, so it is admitted; tests/test_fabric.py::check_f7 depends on that, because {+0.0, -0.0} is the entire reachable domain of the nine `<= 0.0` branches and two distinct readings are what make a hardcoded constant detectable. Tightening the refusal takes F7's second reading away and F7 fails loudly on its own coverage census. All of that I re-verified.
WHAT I ADD. The same test admits NaN and +inf, and those are NOT behaviourally free the way -0.0 is: I measured -0.0 against +0.0 at all eleven levers and got a bit-identical aux_loss, composed loss and gradient absmax-sum, but FAB_BALANCE=nan gives aux_loss nan and 3 of 3 non-finite gradient tensors. So the ruling has three arms, not two:
  (a) -0.0 -- costs nothing today; the whole cost is a minus sign printed beside a mechanism that is off; and F7 currently NEEDS it. Refusing it is defensible but owes F7 a second discriminating value, and there is no third value in a `<= 0.0` domain to reach for.
  (b) NaN -- costs the entire model, silently, with the gate reporting the mechanism off. There is no argument for admitting it that I can see, and refusing it does NOT disturb F7 (measured: the -0.0 arm still builds with my repair applied).
  (c) +inf -- admitted, aux_loss inf, gate FIRED. Same one-line fix.
IF THE OWNER REFUSES (b) AND (c) BUT KEEPS (a), nothing in the suite moves and F7 keeps its teeth. That is the cheapest coherent ruling and it is the one I would put in front of them. If they ALSO refuse (a), the two sentences j_fabric deliberately cross-linked -- the comment on `v < 0.0` in src/fabric/api.py::build and check_f7's docstring -- must be updated together, and F7 needs a second mechanism (their own suggestion: a static hole-tracing rule in tests/test_contract.py::check_k15_gate_reasons_are_self_consistent rather than a runtime sweep here).
